title: Kupowałem czy kupiłem?
note: Aspect, named for the first time, IN THE PAST TENSE ONLY. The whole course to this point has been imperfective by design and the past glosses were written to survive this unit (dynamic = 'was buying', stative = 'knew'), so nothing has to be un-taught here. FOUR twins only: kupować/kupić, robić/zrobić, pić/wypić, czytać/przeczytać. DROPPED the fifth candidate gotować/ugotować — POOL has gotować/gotuje/gotuję but NO past form of gotować has ever been taught, so there is no imperfective past to contrast against; teaching ugotowałem would have meant teaching two new forms at once. FENCED, must not appear anywhere: the PERFECTIVE FUTURE (kupię, zrobię, wypiję, przeczytam) — B1, a different formation, and a2_bedzie has just told the learner the future is będę + infinitive. No table, no distractor, no explain hints that a second future exists. Also note będę itself is NOT in the taught pool at this point (POOL regenerated at the last live node, a2_transport2), so the future is not referenced in Polish at all — the fence is made in English on intro slide 6 ('this choice belongs to the past'). NO PREFIX RULE. The prefixes are z-, wy-, prze- and they are unpredictable; intro slide 2 says so outright and points at the miałem/chciałem precedent — learn the pair whole, never build the second verb from the first. SINGULAR ONLY, both genders in production. Neuter perfectives (kupiło, wypiło) deliberately not taught — nothing demands them and 18 new forms is already the ceiling. FORM BUDGET: wypić carries the full singular paradigm incl. ty-forms (chosen because its imperfective partner piłeś/piłaś IS taught, unlike kupowałeś/czytałaś which are not); kupić, zrobić, przeczytać get I-m / I-f / he / she. 18 new forms total. TIME EVIDENCE verified against POOL: zawsze, często, czasami, wczoraj all present. codziennie is NOT in the pool and was therefore dropped in favour of czasami. Match is deliberately the contrast itself — 6 minimal pairs, imperfective beside perfective — which is what the whole-board reveal is for.

intro.title: Two pasts, not one
intro.body:
Everything you have said about the past so far has described an activity — what was going on, or what you used to do. Kupowałem chleb: I was buying bread, I used to buy bread.

There is a second way to talk about the past, and Polish uses a different verb for it. Kupiłem chleb: I bought the bread. Once. Finished. The bread is in the bag.

English shows this by changing the shape of the verb — was buying / bought. Polish shows it by swapping the verb itself. The two verbs come as a pair, and you learn both together.

The names for them are imperfective — the activity, no endpoint — and perfective — one finished action with a result.
intro.body_pl: Czasownik niedokonany: czynność. Czasownik dokonany: wynik.

rows: I was buying bread. / I used to buy bread.
the activity — going on, or repeated
one action, finished — and I have the bread
I was in the middle of it
I got to the end of it

intro.title: The four pairs — learn them as pairs
intro.body:
Here are the four pairs. Read each line as one item of vocabulary: one meaning, two verbs, two different jobs.

Now look at the front of the perfective verbs. One takes z-, one takes wy-, one takes prze-, and kupić takes nothing at all. There is no rule here and nothing to work out — you cannot predict which piece a verb takes. Polish simply has these pairs.

So learn the pair, the way you learned miałem and chciałem as whole words instead of building them. Never try to make the second verb out of the first.
intro.body_pl: Pary: kupować/kupić, robić/zrobić, pić/wypić, czytać/przeczytać. Uczymy się parami.

intro.title: The endings are the ones you already have
intro.body:
Nothing new happens at the end of the word. Take the perfective verb, cut off the -ć, add -ł, and put on the same person ending you have been using since byłem: -em, -am, -eś, -aś, and nothing at all for he.

wypić is the shortest of the four, so take it as the model: wypi- + ł + ending.

intro.title: The other three
intro.body: Same cut, same endings. The only thing you have to remember is which perfective verb goes with which activity — and you get that from the pairs on the previous slide.
intro.body_pl: Ta sama zasada: kupi-, zrobi-, przeczyta- + ł + końcówka.

intro.title: The time words are your evidence
intro.body:
The words around the verb usually decide for you.

zawsze (always), często (often) and czasami (sometimes) describe a habit — something that happened again and again. A habit has no single finish, so these words take the imperfective verb.

wczoraj (yesterday) points at one occasion. If that occasion finished and left a result, take the perfective verb.

One warning: wczoraj on its own does not force the perfective. Wczoraj czytałem książkę is perfectly good — I was reading a book yesterday, and I may never have finished it.
intro.body_pl: zawsze, często, czasami → niedokonany. wczoraj + wynik → dokonany.

examples.en: I always bought bread at the shop. (m)

intro.title: When you are not sure
intro.body:
Two things worth holding on to.

First: this is a choice you make about the past. It is a choice between two verbs — not a new tense, not a new set of endings. Every sentence in this unit is a past-tense sentence.

Second: if you cannot decide, use the imperfective. It only says the activity happened, which is nearly always true. The perfective makes the extra claim that it was carried through to the end, and that is the part you can be wrong about.

quiz.explain: zawsze describes a habit — the same trip again and again. A habit has no single finish, so it takes the imperfective kupować. kupiłem would report buying bread once.

quiz.prompt: I bought the bread — it is at home now. (m) →
quiz.explain: The bread is at home: the action reached its end and left a result. That is exactly what the perfective kupić says. kupowałem would only report the shopping going on.
zawsze and a single finished action contradict each other. Keep zawsze and the verb has to be the imperfective one: kupowałem.
często means it happened many times, so the verb describes the activity, not one emptied cup. wypiła would name a single finished drink.
wszystko is a finished amount — there is nothing left. A result like that calls for the perfective wypić, and tata is he, so the word stops at the -ł.
czasami — sometimes — is a habit word, and habits are imperfective. wypiłam would point at one particular cup that you finished.
Reaching the end of the book is a result, so the verb is przeczytać. czytałam leaves it open — you were reading, and may have stopped in the middle.

quiz.prompt: Anna made lunch and it was ready →
quiz.explain: The lunch was ready, so the making was carried through: zrobić. Anna is she, so the ending is -a with nothing after it.
często says it happened on many mornings, and many mornings is a habit. Habits take the imperfective: robiła.

quiz.prompt: you drank the coffee up (to a woman) →
quiz.explain: Drank it up — the cup is empty — so wypić, not pić. Then the ordinary -aś you already put on piłaś.

type_items.explain: Do not start from kupowałem. kupić is its own word, so cut its own infinitive: kupi- + ł + em. The -owa- belongs to the other twin.
zrobić takes z-, wypić takes wy-, przeczytać takes prze-. There is no way to work out which one — that is why the pairs are learned whole.
wypić is pić with wy- welded onto the front. Everything after the stem is the ordinary ending you already put on piłeś.
przeczytać means to read something right through to the end. czytałam would say only that you were reading it.

use_items.explain: The bread was bought and the shopping is over — one finished action, so kupić. mama is she, so kupiła.

use_items.prompt_en: Type: Mum used to buy bread.
use_items.explain: used to is a habit, and a habit has no single finish — so the imperfective kupować, exactly as you had it before this unit.

use_items.prompt_en: Type: My brother bought a bike.
Type: Dad drank the beer up.

use_items.explain: zawsze puts you in habit territory, so the verb is pić, not wypić. wypił would mean he emptied one particular glass.

use_items.prompt_en: Type: Yesterday I read the whole book. (m)
Type: Mum was reading a letter.
use_items.explain: was reading is the activity with no end in sight, so czytać. przeczytała would say she finished the letter.

use_items.prompt_en: Type: Yesterday Dad made the soup.
Type: Did you drink the coffee up? (to a man)
use_items.explain: The question is whether the cup is empty, so wypić. Asking Piłeś kawę? would only ask whether you were drinking coffee at all.
